goals.scientificReason: Both languages keep the counted elementary entity explicit. Equal O2-molecule and He-atom amounts are equal entity counts, not equal masses. NaCl is treated as a lattice of ions/formula units; the 0.60 mol total ions do not become 0.60 mol NaCl molecules.

Atom-based molar-mass data and stoichiometric subscripts determine 18 g/mol for H2O and 58 g/mol for Mg(OH)2. Parentheses multiply the entire OH group. Equal amounts of different substances are correctly allowed to have different masses.

u and g refer to the same mass quantity on convenient particle/sample scales. The supplied rounded u conversion and NA produce approximately 44 g per mole CO2 and 4 g for a quarter-mole-equivalent methane count. Neither unit replacement nor exact post-2019 SI numerical identity is asserted.

The fixed Avogadro constant has inverse-mole units. Formula composition factors are separate from NA. The fresh CO2/He comparison reverses the entity-count ranking at total-atom level without altering NA.

Both gases share V,T,p in the first ideal-model case; equal counts and a 16-fold mass ratio follow. The fresh comparison explicitly breaks temperature equality. Equal matched gas-particle counts would still not imply equal total-atom counts for CO2 and He.

Both numerical states are self-consistent rounded ideal-gas school data. The closed nonreacting sample preserves amount, not volume. Selecting each state-specific molar volume is an independent reasoning demand; no derivation from the ideal-gas equation is demanded.

Formula and gas-data routes agree at 44 g/mol for CO2. The fresh state-B route yields 64 g/mol, whereas improperly importing state A yields 128. Compatibility among named formulas is distinguished from unique chemical identification by molar mass alone.

Supplied paired-atom models support molecular notation; Ar provides a monatomic counterexample. Coefficients conserve the specified molecule composition and cannot be replaced by changed subscripts. H2+Cl2→2HCl is correctly conserved.

The neutral Mg/O2 example and the supplied Al/Cu half-equations are numerically and chemically correct. Choosing factors 2 and 3 balances six electrons and total charge +6. However, the independent current D review raised a structural/prerequisite separation finding for the half-equation scope; scientific P correctness is not acceptance of the current atom or authority to narrow away this scope.

CO2 and H2O products support original-sample C/H only against proper dry/CO2-free background controls. The wet blank invalidates attribution of hydrogen while the clear limewater blank supports carbon. Even two controlled positives do not prove absence of O/other elements or a molecular formula.
